prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: A dollar figure for your side's own claims: Just compensation for the land taken; Severance damages to the remainder. The other side's claims could be priced from the record but yours could not, so a net figure would show only what you might pay. Add the amounts you are claiming (rent, balance, contract price, invoices) and run it again.
prediction.likelyOutcome: Boggess will almost certainly recover some just compensation for the taken strip, but the severance-damages claim is meaningfully weakened by admission of the 2016 sale/development evidence, and UDOT's special-benefits offset testimony (now unconstrained by any pretrial exclusion) gives UDOT real leverage to argue the offset should substantially reduce or even eliminate net severance damages. Net recovery is likely to be lower than what Boggess obtained (or sought) in the first, reversed trial, with the ultimate number turning on a battle-of-the-experts the jury will have to resolve.

issues.label: Just compensation for the land taken

outcome.description: On retrial the jury awarded Boggess approximately $330,000 (the opinion gives only this rounded figure) for the value of the condemned property and found no severance damages, after UDOT's expert was allowed to testify to a $2.2 million project-benefit offset. The Court of Appeals held that interstate access and added travel lanes are general benefits that cannot offset severance damages, found the error harmful, reversed the verdict and remanded for a new trial; no fees are discussed.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed for a new trial; no final figure yet.
